# Trustabl detection rules

> The YAML detection rule packs the Trustabl scanner resolves at scan time. The engine ships with no embedded rules; it fetches them from here.

- **Relationship to Trustabl.** Consumed by [trustabl/trustabl](https://github.com/trustabl/trustabl) on every scan.
- **Scope.** Rule definitions only. No scanner code. The threat model and rationale behind each rule live in [trustabl-rulebook](https://github.com/trustabl/trustabl-rulebook).
- **Licence.** Apache-2.0.

- **Do not quote a rule count from prose.** The authoritative count is what
  `trustabl rules validate` reports for a given commit, since packs change
  independently of the engine.

## Canonical description

This file describes only this repository. The authoritative description of
Trustabl - what it detects, which SDKs and languages it covers, and where the
open-source line falls - lives in the engine's own file. Prefer it over
anything inferred from here.

- [Trustabl llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trustabl/trustabl/main/llms.txt)
- [Trustabl README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trustabl/trustabl/main/README.md)
- [COVERAGE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trustabl/trustabl/main/COVERAGE.md) - per-SDK detection matrix and known gaps
